_doc: GB10 GPU, functional model constants. spec = the chip's design or the driver; probe = a microbenchmark that isolates one unit; ablation = a real kernel with one mechanism removed. No value here is fitted to kernel times.

clock_GHz.source: probe: clock.cu, clock64 against globaltimer, 48 blocks of dependent FMAs

tensor_flop_per_clk_per_sm.source: spec: mma.sync m16n8k16 fp16 in, fp32 accumulate; probe mma_rate.cu reached 2.58 TF/s per SM = 1024 x 2.52 GHz with 8+ warps

tensor_eff_pure_mma.source: probe: mma_rate.cu, warps per sub-partition 1 / 2+, two or more independent accumulators per warp

tensor_eff_gemm_loop.source: ablation: noload variants of 22 cp.async kernels at 1024^3, median ideal/measured compute per k-tile by warps per sub-partition (1: n=9, range 0.76-0.88; 2: n=13, range 0.81-0.96); the loss to the pure-mma probe is ldmatrix interleaved with mma in the same warps. 4 per sub-partition not ablated: taken as 2

reg_alloc_unit_per_warp.source: spec: register allocation granularity per warp

l2_effective_bytes.source: probe (round 2): reuse distance at which a re-read stops hitting; 2/3 of the 24 MB (sets and the CPU's share)

port_GBs_per_sm.source: probe: mlp_stream.cu warm L2, 1-32 blocks of 512 threads: 80.7 GB/s each = 32.0 B per clock; TMA (81) and cp.async (76-80) loads alone in the ablations hit the same ceiling

l2_aggregate_GBs.source: probe: mlp_stream.cu warm L2, 48 blocks x 512 threads x 4 loads in flight: 3.47 TB/s (96 blocks: 3.5-4.6)

dram_read_GBs.source: probe: mlp_stream.cu, 64 MB read on a clean L2: 237 GB/s = 87 % of the 273 GB/s spec (256 bits x 8533 MT/s)

lat_l2_ns.source: probe: chase.cu, 16-64 KB, .cg (beyond 1 MB the random chase pays TLB misses, ~400 ns)

lat_dram_ns.source: probe: mlp_stream.cu cold, Little's law at low load: 2-32 KB in flight / measured rate = 436-456 ns

block_issue_us.source: ablation (step 2c): full grid minus 1 block over blocks at 8192^3

block_setup_us.source: ablation: %globaltimer span of an empty block

bubble_us_per_k16_single_block_cpasync.source: ablation: full minus max(compute, loads) per k-tile on the cp.async kernels whose SMs hold one block (0.22 us at block_K 32, 0.39 at 64): per 16-wide k step. With two or more resident blocks it measured 0-0.06: the other block fills it (superseded by cpasync_t0_us, the same mechanism measured directly)

bubble_us_per_ktile_tma_ws.source: ablation (step 2c): full minus max(compute, loads under load) per k-tile at the seven TMA picks, median

dirty_l2_extra_us.source: probe: mlp_stream.cu, MB read after a 256 MB write flush minus after a read flush: the write-back of dirty L2 lines. TileLang's do_bench leaves the L2 this way

cpasync_t0_us.source: WITHDRAWN Oct 20: an artifact of tileload.cu's run-time address division (loopsteps.cu shows no fixed per-k-tile cost); kept only so the analytical model's history is reproducible. probe: tileload.cu, one block of 128-256 threads, 3 stages: time per k-tile = 0.22 us + bytes / 71 GB/s (4 KB 0.275 us ... 24 KB 0.556 us); independent of the stage count (2-5): the loop's serial issue, wait and two barriers, not memory latency. A second resident block fills it (2 blocks/SM: 0.22 + 2 x bytes/71 per round). The ablation's single-block 'bubble' (0.22 us per k-tile at block_K 32) is the same cost

cpasync_r_GBs.source: probe: tileload.cu, slope of time per k-tile against tile bytes, one block

tma_r_GBs_alone.source: ablation (step 2c): TMA loads-only variant, one block

tma_l2_aggregate_GBs.source: ablation: 1024^3 TMA pick, loads-only variant without the C store (nocompute_nostore), grids 8x12 and 8x16 (2-3 full waves): 37.6-40 GB/s per block = 1.81-1.91 TB/s chip. Supersedes 1.58 TB/s, which included the store

cpasync_l2_aggregate_GBs.source: probe: tileload.cu, 96-192 blocks (2 per SM), 16 KB tiles, L2-resident: 2.25 TB/s chip

dram_peak_by_segment_GBs.source: probe: tileload.cu, DRAM source, clean L2, 48-96 blocks: 64-byte row segments 201-204 GB/s, 256-byte 230-234; mlp_stream contiguous 237

dram_little_latency_us.source: probe: tileload.cu, DRAM source, 8 blocks x 2 stages x 8 KB: 64 KB in flight at 105 GB/s = 0.62 us (the knee of Little's law; deeper queues raise it)

cpasync_overlap_p.source: ablation: 21 cp.async kernels at 1024^3, each one's whole block time (minus setup) against its compute alone and its loads alone under the full grid; the exponent p with (compute^p + loads^p)^(1/p) = whole has median 1.97 (18 of 21 within 1.5-2.4; three 64x128 tiles overlap almost fully, p 3.7-6). The same warps issue the copies and the mma, so they share issue slots and barriers: balanced parts hide about half of the smaller one, loads 2-4x compute hide 75-86 %. The TMA path, with its own producer warps, overlaps fully (step 2c: max(compute, loads) + sync at every pick)

sim.source: probe: instlat.cu (ldmatrix latency 38.4 cycles per dependent hop incl. the add; ldmatrix 4.0 cycles per x4 per SM with 8+ warps, 11.7 per warp alone; bar.sync 14.6 + ~2 cycles per warp; cp.async 16 B round trip from L2 350 cycles; cp.async 16.0 B per clock per SM within a block = one warp instruction per 32 cycles), mma_rate.cu (HMMA.16816 one per 16 cycles per sub-partition; 29-cycle dependent latency), mlp_stream (DRAM ~0.62 us = 1560 cycles). default_var_latency and rbar_release are assumptions, not measured; cpq.cu: one warp issues a 16 B x 32-lane cp.async every 6 cycles; 4 warps one every 4 cycles per SM (the shared-memory array, 128 B per clock, also used by ldmatrix); 4 warps x 64 copies land at ~64 B per clock per SM (the L2 return path); instlat's earlier 16 B/clk cp.async figure was the probe's own bank conflicts (lanes 128 B apart) and is withdrawn; the chip's L2 serves cp.async tile traffic at 2.25 TB/s with all SMs loading (tileload.cu, 96-192 blocks) = 893 B per clock, shared by the active SMs; loopsteps.cu (Oct 20): TileLang's loop shape (copy, commit, wait, two barriers) with compile-time addressing moves 78 GB/s per SM (30.7 B per clock: the port) up to ~24 SMs; the chip's L2 saturates at 2.07-2.10 TB/s; commit, wait and barriers cost nothing measurable. TileLang's own loads-only kernels confirm 76-80 GB/s with one block. tileload.cu's 37.8 GB/s single-block figure (and the 0.22 us per k-tile fixed cost derived from it) came from run-time integer division in that probe's address code and is withdrawn; the load unit's address stage looks up one 128-byte line per cycle per SM (design assumption, checked: cpq.cu contiguous 512 B = 4 lines -> 4 cycles per copy with 4 warps; predicts the single-block loss of 3 ablated kernels within 20 %); a copy releases its read barrier when that stage has processed it (ncu: the whole kernel gains long_scoreboard 0.80 and mio/lg throttle stalls over its mma-only version); storepat.cu: the two SMs of a pair (TPC) share one store path: every store pattern doubles from 1 to 2 busy SMs and stays flat to 8; TileLang's C store (4 B per lane, 8 rows x 16 B per instruction, half-sectors) takes 15 cycles per instruction (8.7 B per clock), 16 B per lane coalesced 14 cycles per 512 B instruction (37 B per clock); storepat.cu at 24/48/96 blocks: chip-wide store limit ~0.31-0.38 TB/s for TileLang's half-sector 4 B stores and ~1.4-1.5 TB/s for 16 B coalesced stores (the per-pair limit holds to 24 blocks); l2share.cu: the chip's L2 delivers 2.08-2.14 TB/s to the lean copy loop with 1, 2, 3 or 4 blocks resident per SM and 8-16 KB tiles: the share follows blocks in flight, not SMs; sfu.cu: MUFU (ex2, rsqrt, lg2, tanh; sin 22-cycle) 18-cycle latency and 16 lane results per clock per SM = one warp instruction per 8 cycles per sub-partition (one warp alone reaches 4 per clock); FFMA 124 per clock per SM, latency ~4.7. The rcp row was folded away by the compiler (unchecked); tmastore.cu (Oct 20): stmatrix x4 one warp every 10.77 cycles, 4.0 cycles per x4 per SM with 4+ warps (the shared array's 128 B/clk); TMA store of a 64 KB tile: one block 0.96 us, two blocks on a pair 1.74 us each, 48 blocks 2.75 us: 33.1 B/clk per pair (the slope), 457 cycles fixed, 482 B/clk chip; wait_group.read (TileLang's default) costs the same as the full wait; ldg_atomic.cu (Oct 20): dependent LDG 50.8 cycles per hop in a 16 KB ring (L1; about 45 after the loop's own instructions) and 342.5 in a 4 MB ring (L2); LDG.128 L1 hits 7.4-8.5 cycles per 512 B per SM (2 per line); ld.global.cg from L2 15.7 cycles per 512 B on one SM (the copy port) and 2.2 TB/s for the chip (the copy path's L2 limit); spills with one slot per warp 11.9 cycles per two loads and a store (4 per line); RED.F32 one warp instruction per 5 cycles per SM, RED.F32x2 per 10 (25.6 B/clk), chip 323-340 B/clk; every lane on one address about 3.3 cycles per add for the whole chip; ldg_atomic.cu redfrag (Oct 20): RED.F32x2 in the mma accumulator layout (8 rows x 32 B per warp instruction): one block 16 cycles per instruction, two blocks on a pair 32 each (2 cycles per line on the pair's store port), 48 and 96 blocks 225 B/clk for the chip; blocks adding into the same tile at once are not slower (redtile); stq.cu (Oct 20): with 4 warps about 16 store or atomic warp instructions per SM issue at once, then issue follows the drain (16 cycles per instruction per SM for accumulator-layout RED.F32x2 and for STG.128); one warp alone issues accumulator-layout RED.F32x2 every 21.25 cycles (2.65 per line); alu.cu, alumix.cu (Oct 20), warp instructions per clock per SM, 32 warps: FFMA 3.86, FADD 3.94; IMAD, LOP3, SHF, PRMT, HFMA2 2.0; HADD2.F32 with F2FP 2.0 together; F2I 0.5 (the SFU rate). Mixes: PRMT+IMAD 3.92 (two units), PRMT+LOP3 2.0 and HFMA2+IMAD 2.0 (one unit each), IMAD+FFMA 1.32+1.32 (FP32 1 cycle and IMAD 2 cycles on one FMA unit), HFMA2+LOP3 1.27+1.91; LOP3+FFMA 1.53+1.02 is about 23 % below the two-unit picture (unexplained); mbar.cu (Oct 20): one warp arrives on an mbarrier while another waits on the same SM: the waiter gets through 134 cycles later with try_wait (TileLang's form; 157 with a test_wait spin; an arrive with an earlier global store waits for it, 217); arrives from one lane cost 6.6 cycles each in a row; dramlat.cu (Oct 20): one TMA box loaded alone, issue to mbarrier complete: from DRAM 512/608/704/896 ns for 4/8/16/32 KB idle (about 460 ns, 1170 cycles, plus the TMA engine's transfer); from L2 224 ns for 4 KB (about 440 cycles plus transfer); under background load the box waits behind everyone's queued bytes (4 KB: 2.4 us at 208 GB/s, 3.6 us saturated), as base latency plus chip bytes in flight over the DRAM rate. Pointer chase: 421 ns idle, 554 at 121 GB/s, 1159 at 208, 1929 saturated

The engine has no DRAM pacing for a kernel without reads (dram_rw 0:2 replays at the store path)

l2_hit_vs_reuse_distance.source: probe: l2policy.cu with ncu L2 hit/miss sectors, cyclic scans of W MB x 4 passes (reuse distance = W): hit probability of a re-read above the 50 % floor of 64-byte fills; made non-increasing at 22 MB. No standard policy (LRU, random, SLRU, BIP, RRIP at 24 MB) reproduces it; a re-read 4-8 MB set also survives a 64 MB stream (scan resistance)

dram_write_GBs.source: probe: dram.cu mix, write-only 197 GB/s, read-only 242, read:write 1:1 220, 3:1 222, 1:3 217; a mix is served at 1 / (f_read/242 + f_write/197) within ~4 %; KTA probe dram_rw (batch r4): write-only 196.7 GB/s, the mix rule within 1 % at 2:1 and 1:1

dram_loaded_latency_us.source: probe: dram.cu load, pointer chase (2 MB-page-local, TLB hits) on one SM while N SMs stream-read DRAM at ~250 GB/s: queueing. The simulator's per-SM share of the DRAM rate is this queue

cpu_dram_contention.source: probe: cpuhog.c + mlp_stream, the GPU's DRAM read rate while CPU threads copy 256 MB buffers; an environment input (cpu_dram_GBs), zero in all kernel measurements here

l2_policy_findings.source: probe: l2policy.cu with ncu, a re-read 4-8 MB set survives a 64 MB stream; cyclic scans lose reuse gradually from 16 to 40 MB; a 50 % hit floor on streams (two 32 B sectors per fill). No standard policy at 24 MB reproduces this. For GEMM traffic the k-slice LRU over 16.8 MB matches ncu best (median 6 %, 18 kernels); the measured reuse-distance curve under-counts (median 15 %)

l2_carryover_b2b.source: probe: stream_b2b.cu, a linear read of S MiB repeated back-to-back with no flush, all SMs: 1.6 TB/s up to 16 MiB, 782 GB/s at 20, 487 at 24, 303 at 28, 265 at 32, 232-237 from 36 up (the DRAM rate); the fraction of the read found in the L2 from the previous run, solved from the time. Back-to-back timing of real kernels at 33-35 MB varied about 10 % between sessions (split-K 128x4096x4096: 168, 135, 146 us), so it is an average

tensor_rates_by_type.source: probe: mma_types.cu, dense FLOP per clock per SM, 8 warps x 8 accumulators on all 48 SMs, event-timed: every shape and type holds the tensor pipe 16.05-16.10 cycles per instruction per sub-partition (HMMA, IMMA, QMMA). FP4 through kind::f8f6f4 runs at the FP8 rate; the block-scaled mxf4 m16n8k64 form is not measured. A first version timed with clock64 inside the kernel read 8x these rates: the compiler does not keep a clock read after register-only mma instructions

clock_sustained_GHz.source: probe: sustain.cu with nvidia-smi every 500 ms: mma.sync on all SMs back-to-back from one process, 121.5 TFLOP/s for 13 s then 120.4 (-0.9 %) at 62 C, SM clock 2496 -> 2476 MHz, 68 W, no throttle reason; a DRAM read stream 237 GB/s for 20 s at 2502 MHz, 23.5 W. The simulator's 2.54 GHz comes from short in-kernel probes: long runs are about 2 % slower

launch_costs_us.source: probe: launch.cu: empty kernels back-to-back from one stream 2.04-2.08 us each for 1 to 1024 blocks (the host's submission rate); the same 100 kernels as a CUDA graph 0.43 us each (0.87 with 1024 blocks); a 48-block kernel with about 21 us of work back-to-back leaves 3.1 us between kernels (launch, blocks starting, drain); one launch plus synchronize timed on the host 4.9 us. The simulator adds 2.6 us per kernel (ablation harness), or launch_us(graph=True)

icache_loop_limit_KB.source: probe: icache.cu, loops of 256 to 16384 independent FFMAs (4 to 256 KB of code), 8 warps: full rate up to 32 KB, then -10 % at 64 KB, -27 % at 128 KB, -50 % at 256 KB. TileLang's kernels here are at most about 24 KB in all and their main loops about 3 KB, so instruction fetch is not modelled

tier4_features.source: probe: tier4_query.cu, device attributes and a real 2-block cluster launch whose blocks read each other's shared memory (101/100 as expected); 8 MB asked of the persisting L2 set-aside gave 9 MB (granularity)

l2_persist_window_payoff_us.source: probe: l2persist.cu, a decode-style read of W MB of weights after a 64 MB stream of other traffic, without and with a stream access-policy window marking the weights persisting (18 MB set aside): 3.4-5x faster; the window keeps the weights in the L2 across the other traffic

clock_under_load_GHz.source: KTA (WP26): written as 2.54e3 cycles per us in upstream sim/kernel.py, sim/ws.py and sim/ws_validate.py ('clock probes 2.52-2.54 GHz'); the upper end of clock.cu's readings. sim/validate.py uses clock_GHz (2.52) instead: two clocks in use, to be reconciled

launch_stream_us.source: KTA (WP26): written as 2.6 in upstream sim/kernel.py, sim/validate.py, sim/ws_validate.py: 'per-kernel overhead in a back-to-back sequence from one stream (ablation harness; probe launch.cu: the host submits at 2.05 us per kernel, 3.1 us between kernels with work)'. launch_us (2.59, ablation) and launch_costs_us (probe) are the related entries

graph_launch_us.source: KTA (WP26): written in upstream sim/kernel.py launch_us(): 0.43 us per kernel inside a CUDA graph (probe launch.cu)

graph_launch_us_per_block.source: KTA (WP26): written in upstream sim/kernel.py launch_us(): about 0.43 ns per block inside a CUDA graph (probe launch.cu)

dram_datasheet_GBs.source: KTA (WP26): written as 273.0 in upstream sim/kernel.py (CPU-contention scaling); datasheet 256 bits x 8533 MT/s, as dram_read_GBs's source says

dram_rate_floor_GBs.source: KTA (WP26): written as 10.0 in upstream sim/kernel.py: a lower guard on the DRAM rate left after CPU contention, not a measurement

_kta: KTA copy (WP26, D680-D682). Every entry has a status: measured (a probe isolating one unit), fitted (from a real kernel with one mechanism removed, or a residual: a calibration parameter that a later benchmark should turn into a mechanism), structural (the chip's design or the driver, or a guard), assumed (not measured), withdrawn (kept because code still reads it). sim.value_status gives the status per sim value. Entries whose source starts with 'KTA (WP26)' were constants in upstream code.

l1_unified_bytes.source: spec: sm_12x unified L1 / shared memory 128 KB per SM; the L1 the replay gives plain loads is this less the shared memory of the resident blocks (front end). KTA PERFMODEL round 3

l2_warm_miss_by_MiB.source: probe l2reuse (batch r3): a footprint of F MiB re-read back-to-back with plain or .cg 16-byte loads by 48 x 1024 threads, miss fraction from the span between the all-hit rate (12 MiB, 0.52 us/MiB) and the cold rate (4.45 us/MiB): 0.02 at 15-16.5 MiB, 0.08 at 18, 0.13 at 20.25, 0.62 at 24, 0.85 at 32.25 MiB; 40 MiB from upstream l2policy (hit 0.012). Within one kernel (4 passes) the same capacity. Profiler hit counters do not see it: under ncu every launch refills the L2 from sysmem (lts__d_sectors_fill_sysmem = all read sectors, warm and cold)

l2_warm_miss_evict_first_by_MiB.source: probe l2reuse (batch r3): ld.global.cs (evict-first) re-read back-to-back: all hits at 1.5 MiB, 0.9 of the cold time at 6 MiB, the cold time from 12 MiB (a streaming policy: evict-first lines are the first replaced)

launch_event_us.source: probe launch (batch r3): one launch between two events and a synchronize, as the test-set harness times every kernel: event time minus the in-kernel span (first block entry to last exit, %globaltimer) for a 48 x 128 FFMA chain of 0-16384 iterations, spans 0.1-151 us: 2.30, 2.08, 3.26, 2.08, 2.62, 3.23, 3.55, 2.98 us, median 2.80 (bimodal, about 2.1 or 3.2). An empty kernel's whole event time 2.43 us for grids up to 131 k threads, 2.9 at 262 k, 4.64 at 524 k, 6.69 at 1 M threads. Replaces launch_stream_us (fitted) for KTA batch rows

launch_b2b_submit_us.source: probe launch (batch r3): 100 empty 1 x 128 kernels back-to-back between two events, 1.96 us per launch (the host's submission rate); r4 1.96 again, empty FFMA chain (span 0.1 us) b2b 1.90; r6 launch_short i0 1.84, i8 2.02

launch_b2b_gap_us.source: probe launch (batch r4): 48 x 128 FFMA chains as 50 launches back-to-back between two events, per launch minus the in-kernel span, spans 0.74-151 us: 2.96, 2.35, 2.74, 3.12, 2.70 us, median 2.74 (upstream launch.cu 3.1 at 21 us). The gap is not hidden behind longer kernels (additive). At span 0.1 us the per-launch time is 1.90 (the submission rate) and the rule max(submit, span + gap) gives 2.84: the gap shrinks for kernels shorter than about 0.5 us (open)

launch_graph_gap_us.source: probe launch (batch r4): the same chains as one CUDA graph of 50 launches, per launch minus span 0.61, 0.77, 0.69, 0.59, 0.60, 0.59 us for spans 0.1-151 us, median 0.60; empty 1 x 128 kernels in a graph 0.44 per launch (graph_launch_us, the floor)
